title: An administrator account is taken over
description: Stolen credentials on a privileged account would give an attacker control of production and identity systems.
treatment: Require phishing-resistant MFA for every privileged account

title: People keep access after they leave or change roles
description: Former staff or stale permissions could be used to reach customer data.

title: Customer data is exposed from cloud storage
description: A public or unencrypted bucket could leak data without any attack.
treatment: Block public access; encrypt every bucket

title: Malicious activity goes unnoticed
description: Without logs on critical systems, an incident can't be detected or investigated.
treatment: Logging on every critical system; protected audit trail

title: Staff fall for phishing or social engineering
description: Untrained staff are the most common way attackers get in.
treatment: Annual security training with a 95% completion target

title: A vendor breach exposes our data
description: A critical vendor renewed without a current security review could carry unknown risk.
treatment: Review critical vendors before every renewal

title: One user reads another team's records
description: Missing database access rules would let any signed-in user read everything.
treatment: Row Level Security on every table

title: Laptops without disk encryption
close_note: Sample history: evidence showed 100% of laptops encrypted.

title: Shared admin password in a spreadsheet
close_note: Sample history: credential rotated and spreadsheet deleted.

title: Backups never restore-tested
close_note: Sample history: restore test passed and documented.

title: Unreviewed open-source licenses
close_note: Sample history: scanner added to every pull request.
